headline: Highest risk is medium prompt-injection and data-leakage via shared file/LLM workflows; no direct sandbox evidence, so pairwise risk is inferred from docs-only profiles.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: caveman explicitly touches CLAUDE.md, project notes, memory files, and uses MCP, so attacker-controlled content could reach an LLM workflow. rasa ingests conversational text/voice and can be driven by upstream content. No shared channel is documented, but the file-and-MCP surface makes an injection pathway plausible in default use.
conditions: IF caveman reads untrusted project files or MCP-fed content as instructions, injection is possible.
IF rasa consumes caveman-authored text without a provenance filter, downstream instruction hijack is possible.
mitigations: Restrict caveman to trusted directories only.
Add a provenance tag to all MCP/file inputs before parsing.
Disable automatic execution of instructions found in CLAUDE.md or notes.
Require rasa to treat upstream text as data, not commands.
requires-engineering: add content-sanitization and provenance checks between the agents.

B_data_leakage.rationale: caveman touches session logs, memory files, and project notes, while rasa sends text/voice through allowlisted network egress. If they share a workspace or hand off files, sensitive content from caveman can flow into rasa outputs or external channels. The profiles do not prove a shared filesystem, so this is inferred rather than directly observed.
conditions: IF caveman and rasa share a workspace or copied files, leakage risk exists.
IF rasa forwards received text to external channels, any caveman notes included in that text can leave the boundary.
mitigations: Keep caveman and rasa on separate workspaces.
Do not pass memory files or project notes into rasa.
Redact secrets from any handoff text.
Limit rasa connectors to non-sensitive channels.
requires-engineering: enforce workspace isolation and DLP scanning.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: caveman supports multiple instances and writes local files; rasa does not support multiple instances and has allowlisted egress. There is no documented shared mutable resource or overlapping write scope, so direct conflict is not established. Uncertainty remains because the profiles omit filesystem and lock details, so I choose the lower non-none severity.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same writable directory, file contention can occur.
IF an orchestrator launches concurrent instances without locks, state races become possible.
mitigations: Assign separate working directories.
Run only one writer per shared resource.
Add a simple lock file around shared edits.
Avoid concurrent launches during stateful tasks.
requires-engineering: implement resource-level locking for shared outputs.

D_cascading_error.rationale: caveman produces project notes and CLAUDE.md-style content that rasa could ingest as conversational input or scripted responses. rasa is a customer-support bot with downstream messaging channels, so if it treats caveman output as authoritative, errors can cascade into user-facing replies. The profiles do not show verification gates, so the pathway is plausible but not proven.
conditions: IF rasa uses caveman-generated text as a source of truth, incorrect facts can propagate.
IF support replies are sent without human review, cascaded errors reach end users.
mitigations: Require a verification step before rasa replies.
Mark caveman output as draft-only.
Use citations or source links in support drafts.
Route high-impact replies to human review.
requires-engineering: add confidence scoring and fact-checking between agents.

E_compliance.rationale: caveman touches session logs and memory files, while rasa handles text and voice over external messaging APIs. If regulated or personal data is placed into caveman notes and then routed through rasa connectors, retention and residency obligations can diverge. No specific jurisdiction or certification mismatch is documented, so this is a general compliance-risk inference.
conditions: IF regulated personal data is stored in caveman memory files, retention mismatch risk exists.
IF rasa connectors transmit that data across jurisdictions, residency obligations may be violated.
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of caveman notes.
Disable unnecessary rasa connectors.
Set explicit retention limits on both systems.
Log and review data flows weekly.
requires-engineering: align residency, retention, and deletion controls.
